Thanks for the context — this is doable but needs scoping. A few clarifying questions for the customer (Vanessa / Ben, can you confirm before I send):

- Audit export: do they need full token-level content or metadata (trace id, model id, timestamps, request/response hashes)? Full token-level export may trigger PHI concerns. We should propose hashed content + original-request redaction and clarify retention (30/90/365 days).
- Residency: 90 days of warm pool is fine as a short-term ramp if we restrict to specific model variants and agree on throughput windows. Do they require hard isolation (dedicated nodes) or affinity (preferred placement) with fallbacks?
- SLA: are they asking for P50 2s in contract or operational target? Contractual latency SLAs have broader implications for penalties.

I can draft 2 options: "Assured affinity" (preferred but not fully isolated) and "Dedicated residency" (reserved nodes for SLA). Will iterate after internal engineering feasibility.

—Monica

High-level engineering take: we can support both flavors but with different operational costs and lead times. Notes:  

- Affinity + warm cache (soft guarantee): low lift. We can recommend a staffing plan and a warm pool config to achieve 2s P50 at 200 rps for the fine-tuned variant. No contractual SLA penalties.
- Dedicated residency (hard isolation): requires reserved capacity (Dedicated) and a short provisioning lead time (2–3 weeks for GPU reservations and qualification). Cost uplift is ~2.3x vs. hosted.
- Audit export: we can produce daily parity exports (JSONL) with metadata + hashed tokens. If they require raw token content, legal sign-off and additional encryption controls are needed (KMS/HSM changes).

Action items for scoping: engineering runbook for warm pool, proposed pricing delta for Dedicated, and compliance's view on raw-export PHI. I can map out a minimal canary to validate latency over one week.

—Markus
SVP, Inference Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production readiness + timeline questions after demo

Compliance input: we cannot provide raw token-level exports containing PHI. Options we can offer to Oakridge (to be included in SOW):

1) Daily metadata export (trace id, model id, timestamps, request/response hash) — standard, no PHI exposure. Retention options: 90/365 days.
2) Redacted token export with deterministic hashing and per-customer KMS wrapping — possible but requires 1-week legal/compliance review + updated KMS policy and extra support for key rotation.

Recommend we present both and highlight that raw token retention is not permitted without additional contractual guardrails. I'll coordinate with Security for one-page guidance to attach to SOW.

—Laura
Head of Compliance | Redwood Inference

Claire — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and two options for inclusion in the SOW so Procurement can decide: 

Option A — Affinity + Warm Pool (default, faster):
- 90-day warm residency by affinity to specified model variant (preferred placement with fallback).
- Daily metadata export (trace id, model id, timestamps, hashes); retention: 90 days.
- Provisioning: immediate; can be in-scope for Hosted (no Dedicated uplift).
- Commercial: standard Hosted rate + 15% premium for warm pool support.

Option B — Dedicated Residency (contractual SLA):
- Reserved capacity with node-level isolation for 90 days.
- Daily redacted-token export with per-customer KMS wrapping (requires DocuSign addendum + 1-week compliance window).
- Provisioning lead: 2–3 weeks.
- Commercial: Dedicated pricing (2.3x Hosted) + implementation fee.

Next steps we propose: pick Option A to unblock a Q1 pilot, then if Oakridge wants contractual isolation move to Option B during quarter 1. I've attached the redline SOW and pricing sheet showing both paths. Monica/Markus/Laura will follow up on runbook and compliance note.

If this looks right, procurement — can you confirm which option you prefer by Dec 20 so we can finalize the SOW?
